item.title: In, on, at for time
item.explanation_text: Use at for clock times and a few fixed phrases: at 7 o'clock, at noon, at night, at the weekend (British English). Use on for days and dates: on Monday, on 21 March, on my birthday, on Friday morning. Use in for longer periods: in the morning, in July, in winter, in 2010. Don't use in, on or at before this, next, last, every, today, tomorrow or yesterday: I saw her last Monday. We're leaving next week.
item.contrast_text: Compare: in the morning, but on Monday morning. at night, but in the evening.
item.common_error_pattern: Using in with days and dates ('in Monday'), or putting a preposition before next, last or every ('on next week').

examples.bad: I'll call you on next Friday.
